item.title: How the Iranian Economy Actually Works
item.description: The revolution changed everything.

item.title: Odd Lots: How the Iranian Economy Actually Works (Podcast)
item.description: After the Iranian Revolution of 1979, the country’s new leaders — religious and political — promised to redistribute the country’s wealth and made moves to make Iran independent from western influence and business interests. In the decades since, Iran’s economy completely transformed, and it is closer to what Yeganeh Torbati and Bozorgmehr Sharafedin describe as a “mafia state,” where fealty to various factions is baked into the country’s political economy. item.title: US-Iran Talks ‘Ongoing’ to Normalize Situation, Pakistan Says
item.description: The negotiations between the US and Iran are “ongoing” to restore stability, particularly in the Strait of Hormuz, Pakistan’s Foreign Ministry spokesperson Tahir Andrabi said at a weekly briefing in Islamabad.

item.title: Foxtons Sales Fees Drop 13% Showing London Housing Rut
item.description: Foxtons Group Plc has seen revenue from advising on home sales plunge, the latest sign of the downturn gripping the London housing market.

item.title: INR/USD: India Central Bank Sold About $7 Billion to Defend Rupee on Friday
item.description: India’s central bank sold about $7 billion to defend the rupee last Friday, in what was one of its largest direct interventions in months, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Saudi Economy Shrinks Most Since 2020 as War Roils Oil Exports
item.description: Saudi Arabia’s economy saw its sharpest quarterly contraction since the Covid-19 pandemic, as the US-Israeli war against Iran poses challenges to the vital oil industry.

item.title: LSEG Boosts Guidance as AI Rollout Adds to Record First Half
item.description: London Stock Exchange Group Plc raised its guidance for the year and said its push into artificial intelligence was gaining momentum with customers.

item.title: Anglo Cashes In on Copper as Strategy Shift Starts to Pay Off
item.description: Anglo American Plc saw a steep jump in earnings, driven by the copper mines that it’s put at the center of its new strategy.

item.title: Rolls-Royce Lifts Outlook Again as Demand Soars for Engines
item.description: Rolls-Royce Holdings Plc raised its full-year guidance for a second time as the UK’s largest manufacturer earned more from selling engines for widebody planes, military hardware and artificial intelligence.

item.title: Shell Profit Surges to $9.8 Billion on Oil Trading and Refining Gains
item.description: Shell Plc said its second-quarter profit soared to the highest since the outbreak of the Ukraine war as conflict in the Middle East drives a boom in trading and refining for the world’s energy majors.

item.title: BMW’s Carmaking Profit Beats Expectations on Cost Cuts
item.description: BMW AG’s profit from carmaking in the second quarter was slightly better than expected after the German company reduced spending and demand for new models was strong.

item.title: French Economy Rebounds With 0.2% Growth in Second Quarter
item.description: France’s economy returned to growth in the second quarter, avoiding a recession as domestic demand picked up and exports rebounded.

item.title: Modi’s Rival Targets Key Minister Shah Over Student Crackdown
item.description: India’s main opposition Congress Party has sought the resignation of Home Minister Amit Shah, a close aide of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, over the police crackdown on student protesters in New Delhi last week.

item.title: Australia Online Regulator Starts Civil Proceedings Against Telegram
item.description: Australia’s eSafety regulator has commenced civil penalty proceedings in Federal Court against the provider of Telegram for the messaging service’s alleged failure to detect and remove pro-terror material.

item.title: Chinese Chip Stocks Plunge as Investors Rotate Away From Tech
item.description: Chinese tech stocks plunged on Thursday, led by high-flying semiconductor names, as concerns over stretched valuations and crowded positioning intensified a rotation out of one of this year’s best-performing sectors.

item.title: Base Metals Advance as Fed Rate Pause Eases Demand Concerns
item.description: Copper, aluminum and zinc rose after the US Federal Reserve left interest rates unchanged, easing concerns over industrial demand.

item.title: Pakistan’s Fintech Abhi Plans Microfinance Bank IPO This Month
item.description: Pakistan’s fintech group Abhi is preparing to launch an initial public offering of its microlender this month, according to its founder, as it seeks to capitalize on the nation’s busiest year for listings.

item.title: Peso Slump, Electronics Demand Lift Philippine Exports to Record High
item.description: Philippine exports rose to a record in June on the back of strong electronics demand and a weak peso.

item.title: British Shoppers Tap Savings Buffers to Ride Out Economic Pain
item.description: Since the pandemic, British families have been building a financial buffer for when they might need it most. That time seems to have come.

item.title: Australia, NZ Seen Switching to Next-Day Settlement by 2030
item.description: New Zealand and Australia are expected to join a global transition to next-day settlement of stock transactions within five years, once key clearing and settlement systems are ready, according to a senior banker.

item.title: Japan’s Two-Year Bond Sale Draws Weaker Demand on Rate Hike Bets
item.description: Japan’s two-year government bond auction Thursday saw lower demand than the 12-month average amid growing expectations of central bank tightening.

item.title: Chubu and Tokyo Electric Slide as High Fuel Costs Curb Profits
item.description: Chubu Electric Co. and Tokyo Electric Power Co. shares fell after the Japanese utilities said their quarterly earnings were impacted by surging fuel costs, which coincided with the end of a power supply agreement.

item.title: Malaysia’s Bond Market Outflow May Slow on Fiscal, Rate Outlooks
item.description: Global investors’ retreat from Malaysian debt may ease, supported by the country’s relatively healthy finances and efforts to ease inflationary pressures, market participants said.

item.title: Japan’s Takaichi Calls for Food Sales Tax Cut to 1% for 2 Years
item.description: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi has decided to temporarily cut the sales tax on food and soft drinks to 1% from April next year, a top executive in the ruling party said, in a sign the premier is moving ahead with a key pledge after months of political deadlock.

item.title: India Seeks Sunflower Oil Alternatives on Black Sea Disruptions
item.description: India, the world’s top sunflower oil buyer, is rushing to secure supplies of alternate vegetable oils as attacks in the Black Sea region disrupt imports and its own crops falter due to weak monsoon rains.

item.title: India’s Nifty Continues to Hit Technical Resistance at 200-Day Moving Average
item.description: The trend shows that the benchmark has yet to convincingly reclaim its long-term momentum.

item.title: China’s Launch of Advanced Hypersonic Missile Hints at Wider Use
item.description: China revealed for the first time the launch of the YJ-20 missile from a smaller destroyer, paving the way for one of its most advanced hypersonic weapons to be deployed on the fleet of vessels.

item.title: China’s Coal Demand Gets Boost as Heatwave Lifts Aircon Use
item.description: China’s thermal coal prices are rebounding as a mild start to summer finally gives way to hotter weather, boosting air-conditioner usage and power demand.

item.title: Korean Stocks’ Record Rout Fails to Tempt Global Investors
item.description: South Korea’s stock market is displaying what would appear to be clear dip‑buying signs: July’s record 33% plunge that has left the benchmark Kospi at its cheapest valuation ever.

item.title: INR/USD: India’s $32 Billion Forex Inflows Yet to Boost Rupee
item.description: India’s plan to boost inflows into the country has got off to a strong start, with the central bank Governor Sanjay Malhotra saying banks have garnered $32 billion under the various measures announced.
